children: Advanced Micro Devices, the AI-chip and processor designer

, rebounded approximately 3.0% to $508 Tuesday morning as semiconductor stocks fought back from Monday's sharp AI-driven selloff. AMD had dropped more than 4% in the previous session, but the recovery suggests investors are separating warnings about the pace of advanced AI development from any concrete slowdown in chip demand. The valuation picture remains far more aggressive: the chart shows AMD trading 80.32% above its $281.72 GF Value estimate, leaving little room for execution mistakes at the current price.

AMD's second-quarter results explain why investors are willing to pay up. Revenue surged 50% year over year to $11.54 billion, while data-center revenue more than doubled to $6.7 billion as EPYC CPUs and Instinct AI accelerators gained traction. Management is now guiding for roughly $13 billion in third-quarter revenue with an adjusted gross margin near 56%, putting another strong growth quarter within reach if hyperscaler and enterprise AI spending holds.

The numbers also show exactly where the risk sits. Data centers already account for roughly 58.1% of AMD's revenue, and reaching the third-quarter target would require sales to climb another 12.7% sequentially. That concentration can turbocharge earnings while AI infrastructure spending remains strong, but it cuts both ways if deployment schedules start slipping. Tuesday's rebound brings the optimism back quickly; at $508 and more than 80% above GF Value, AMD now needs its operating performance to keep moving just as fast.

title: AMD Rebounds 3% as Its 58% AI Engine Faces a Pause
